PullRequest.Title: feat(chat-lib): add editor-agnostic NES language context provider (alternative to #349299)
PullRequest.Body:

## Why

This is an alternative to #349299, opened so we can compare the two designs. Both let chat-lib NES embedders supply language context, so the Copilot language server can pass JetBrains PSI declarations into NES prompts. @FantasticCK, thanks for the original change. I'd like your opinion on whether this API works for the language server. In particular: does the language server already have `Copilot.ContextProvider` implementations it wants to reuse for NES, and does it need traits? Both can be added without breaking anything (see Tradeoffs).

## What changed

- `INESProviderOptions.languageContext` takes an `INESLanguageContextProvider`. NES calls it with the exact document text it prompts with, the cursor as a UTF-16 offset and a deadline. The provider streams `{ uri, value }` snippets back. Snippets that arrive after the deadline are dropped.
- xtab now gets language context from a new internal `INextEditLanguageContextService`. In VS Code that service runs the same code xtab ran before, moved into `ContextProviderLanguageContextService`. In chat-lib it wraps the embedder's provider.

## Tradeoffs

How this differs from #349299, and why:

- **No `vscode.TextDocument` in the embedder API.** #349299 passes the embedder's `ILanguageContextProviderService` a VS Code `TextDocument`. Here the embedder gets plain strings and numbers.
- **No second workspace.** In #349299 the embedder also supplies an `IWorkspaceService`, and xtab reads the text, offset and version from it while the cursor comes from the NES snapshot. The two copies can drift apart. Running the #349299 test with logging, I saw the provider receive `class Point` while the prompt used the edited `class Point3D`. Here the request is built only from the snapshot.
- **No internal types.** Implementing `ILanguageContextProviderService` means building internal `ContextItem` values, which use an enum and a `URI` class chat-lib doesn't export. Snippets here have `uri` and `value` only, the two snippet fields the prompt reads.
- **Snippets only, for now.** The NES prompt also renders traits, such as a language version, but this API can't supply them yet. Adding a trait variant to the result type later won't break existing providers.
- **No direct reuse of `Copilot.ContextProvider` objects.** VS Code's own context providers use the `vscode` API and never run in chat-lib. That's true of #349299 as well. A provider the embedder already wrote against the public Copilot context-provider API, for completions for example, needs a small adapter to plug into NES. chat-lib could ship that adapter later, built on the same registry and match function completions uses, without breaking anything.
- **No version.** chat-lib's document version is a local counter, not the IDE's, and pairing a version with the right text needs more plumbing. The text is authoritative instead. A provider that can't describe that text, for example on a speculative request, yields nothing. An optional version can be added later without breaking anything.
- **Cross-file edits stay off.** In #349299 a supplied workspace service also turns them on.

## Blast Radius

- chat-lib NES embedders: one new optional option. Without it, behavior is unchanged.
- VS Code NES: the language-context code moved into a service, with the same inputs and outputs.
- `ILanguageContextProviderService` is unchanged, so chat-lib completions embedders are unaffected.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run src/lib/vscode-node/test/nesProvider.spec.ts`: 14 passed. The new tests fail when the provider gets the pre-edit text, when the deadline isn't enforced, and when the provider is ignored.
- `npx vitest run src/extension/xtab src/extension/inlineEdits src/lib src/platform/inlineEdits`: 2,587 passed and 11 failed. The same 11 fail on `main` without this change (`DiffServiceImpl: worker file not found`).
- `tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json` in `extensions/copilot` and `oxlint` on the changed files: clean.
- `npm run extract-chat-lib`, then chat-lib's `tsc` and its copy of the spec: 14 passed.
- Not run: end to end with the language server and the IntelliJ plugin, or NES in a running VS Code.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new collector checks cancellation but not elapsed time, raceTimeout uses setTimeout, and cancellation occurs only after the race completes. Immediately yielding async iterators drain through microtasks before timers can run. The awaited prompt-gathering call path and per-snippet allocations are explicit; batch sizes and elapsed latency are not measured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Iterator processing CPU, URI objects, and LanguageContextEntry objects retained in the per-request items array
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For each actual uncached/unjoined NES generation, work and temporary entry storage grow with all N immediately yielded snippets, rather than the prefix obtainable before the deadline. NES result-cache hits and joined requests do not invoke a separate collector.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Blocked prompt/network issuance and increased event-loop latency and allocation/GC pressure beyond the configured context budget
Findings.PreviousBehavior: chat-lib registered NullWorkspaceService and NullLanguageContextProviderService, so the old XtabProvider language-context path returned undefined without invoking an embedder or collecting snippets. The unchanged VS Code collector is not the subject of this finding.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new embedder adapter adds an awaited streaming collector and treats a timer race as its only deadline enforcement, allowing ready snippets to bypass the intended time bound and accumulate before downstream prompt clipping.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 632-637 consume and allocate entries with only a cancellation check; added line 641 relies on a timer race, while added lines 643-644 cancel the token only after that race finishes. These lines newly create the unbounded-by-deadline collection path in chat-lib.
Findings.Title: Enforce the deadline while consuming ready snippets
Findings.Impact: With language context enabled, an embedder streaming a large cached declaration batch can delay the next-edit request and other work on the same event loop by consuming and allocating the entire batch, including snippets produced after the supplied deadline. This also occurs when prior prompt preparation has already exhausted the debounce budget.
Findings.Evidence: EmbedderLanguageContextService collects each snippet with URI.parse and items.push (lines 632-637), checking only cts.token.isCancellationRequested. Its timeout is raceTimeout(collect(), request.timeBudgetMs) at line 641; util/vs/base/common/async.ts:159-169 implements that timeout with setTimeout. An async generator yielding cached snippets without an intervening task-level wait therefore keeps scheduling microtasks, preventing the timeout and finally's cancellation from running until the batch finishes. XtabProvider.gatherContextAndClipCurrentFile awaits language context before prompt construction and endpoint.makeChatRequest2. DelaySession.getDebounceTime can return zero, and prompt token clipping happens only after collection.
Findings.Recommendation: Store the absolute deadline and check Date.now() against it before starting/advancing collection and before accepting each snippet, alongside cancellation. Race against the remaining time rather than restarting the full budget after provider setup, and retain the existing finally cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: VS Code NES gathers registered language context before issuing a prediction
Scenarios.CriticalPath: XtabProvider awaits getAndProcessLanguageContext during gatherContextAndClipCurrentFile, then gathers neighbors, builds/clips the prompt, finishes remaining debounce, and issues the existing streaming chat request. Context timeout fallback ignore checks can extend this wait, but that behavior already existed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read cached language-server results and optionally await an already-running typescript.tsserverRequest context computation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: NES getContext issues zero fresh TS6 context IPC calls; it may join one matching cache-population request. Cache population itself uses one context command when server work is required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical registered-provider resolver, cached-results path, and server-request joining before extraction into the new service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cached results are immediately available; joining an existing computation waits at most the provider's existing cache-population race window, subject to the outer context timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Search for and read local .copilotignore files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared initialization across callers: one search per applicable workspace folder and reads for discovered ignore files. Failed initialization is retried after the existing five-second interval.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old XtabProvider performed the same isCopilotIgnored checks and awaited the same shared initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: First enabled content-exclusion decision awaits initialization; warm decisions reuse its promise.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve repository roots and fetch URLs through the git service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold unresolved URI checks can each resolve metadata until repository-root caching is populated; subsequent files under a cached root skip the lookup. Unsettled repositories can retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same primary/additional URI checks and repository-root cache behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs inside the existing awaited snippet ignore decision.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch content-exclusion rules for missing or expired remote keys and organization rules
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Distinct missing remote keys plus the non-git organization key are coalesced per key and dispatched in batches of at most 10, at most 5 batches concurrently. Not one HTTP call per snippet; warm unexpired rules issue none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical rule-key caching, 50ms batching window, shared limiter and middleware backoff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each ignore decision awaits only its required keys; existing timeout collection and fallback placement are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read up to 1KiB of source for regex content-exclusion checks, using an open text buffer where available
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one header read per evaluated URI when regex rules require content and no reusable verdict short-circuits it; shared file-read concurrency is 10. Content-hash caching avoids repeated regex evaluation but does not necessarily avoid obtaining contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same header reads and checks; merely moved out of XtabProvider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of the existing awaited snippet ignore decision.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue and stream the NES model prediction
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per actual generation attempt; existing retries/cursor-jump attempts can add requests. Result-cache hits and joined calls do not independently issue requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same endpoint and issuance order relative to context gathering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: First edit requires streamed model output after context and prompt preparation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P matching NES providers; N yielded snippets; U total primary/additional snippet URI checks; R distinct repository remotes. These are not equivalent cardinalities.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: P resolvers run through Promise.allSettled. Collector processes snippets serially; primary/additional URI checks for a snippet run concurrently. Content-exclusion HTTP batches contain at most 10 remote keys with at most 5 batches active; header reads have a shared limit of 10. Existing NES request joining and replacement cancellation are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider matching and workspace-document lookup remain unchanged. The inspected TS6 provider yields character-budgeted cached context and can join an existing cache-population server request rather than issuing a new server computation. Ignore initialization is shared, successful repository roots/rules and suitable verdicts are cached; rules expire after 30 minutes and empty rulesets are cached. Failed rules remain uncached with existing middleware backoff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that production VS Code work is an extraction with unchanged provider invocation, ignore fan-out, caches and scheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider counts, repository/cache state, filesystem latency and server response times depend on the workspace. No measured durations were available.
Scenarios.Verdict: No new performance regression established for the VS Code implementation; potentially expensive timeout/fan-out behavior is pre-existing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or use chat-lib NES without an embedder language-context provider, or with context and recording disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Service setup stores a lightweight optional provider reference without invoking it. Disabled context/recording skips gathering; an omitted provider returns undefined immediately. Existing model selection, prompt preparation and prediction remain the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue the existing NES prediction request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per actual generation attempt, zero independent calls for result-cache hits or joined requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same request boundary without language context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for uncached suggestions; no added language-context delay.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Actual NES generation attempts, document size and existing history; no language-context snippet collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No context tasks start. Existing pending-request replacement and speculative request management remain unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing result-cache hits, negative/no-edit entries and in-flight request joining remain upstream of XtabProvider. No new context cache is allocated. StringText already owns a cached position transformer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both skip paths are explicit, and setup does not call provideContext or initialize a second workspace.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No runtime measurements; the new setup allocation is a single small service object per NES facade.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression when the optional integration is unused; no new subprocess, IPC, filesystem or database operation is present on this changed path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Chat-lib uncached NES prediction consumes embedder snippets from cold asynchronous or warm ready-to-yield context
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new EmbedderLanguageContextService is awaited before prompt construction and model issuance. Cold asynchronous collection usually returns on completion, cancellation or timeout. Ready-to-yield async iterators can monopolize microtasks and prevent the timer from enforcing the deadline.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the embedder once and pull its AsyncIterable of context snippets
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One invocation and up to N iterator pulls per actual generation; no local grouping/deduplication. Concrete host IPC or filesystem operations are not provided by this repository and are not assumed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: NullWorkspaceService/NullLanguageContextProviderService caused the old chat-lib context path to return undefined with zero embedder invocations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited when prompt language context is enabled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse each snippet URI and allocate/store internal snippet and LanguageContextEntry objects
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One URI conversion and entry allocation for every accepted snippet. With a ready-to-yield stream, all N can be accepted even after the deadline; downstream token clipping does not bound this buffer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before language-context collection resolves and before the prompt can be sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue and stream the existing NES prediction request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per actual attempt; the context adapter adds no per-snippet HTTP prediction requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same prediction request but without embedder collection ahead of it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Issuance is delayed by the new awaited collector; deadline bypass can extend that delay with total batch size.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N snippets emitted by one embedder invocation per actual unjoined generation, including repeated URIs; collection performs no deduplication. The later prompt token budget restricts rendering, not collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One sequential collector per actual generation, not one provider call per snippet. Upstream cancellation/joining remains in place; the adapter adds no global limiter. Timer completion cancels the child token in finally, but a microtask-only stream prevents that timer from running until collection finishes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No adapter-level cache exists. Embedder caching is external and unspecified; a warm provider may yield cached results immediately. NES result-cache hits and same-state in-flight joins avoid an additional provider invocation. Document text is passed by reference locally and its transformer is already cached, not newly copied or rescanned here.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added loop has no wall-clock deadline check, raceTimeout is implemented with setTimeout, and each iteration allocates before any downstream token cap. JavaScript microtask scheduling establishes the timeout bypass.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The embedder implementation and largest context batch are external, so prevalence, CPU time and allocation volume are not measured. Immediate cached async-generator yields are a supported, realistic input.
Scenarios.Verdict: Submitted one medium-severity finding for deadline-bypassing collection and allocation. Ordinary asynchronous context work is intentional; the finding concerns work continuing past the intended bound.

Scenarios.Scenario: Chat-lib speculative prediction, recorder-only context collection, cancellation and late provider output
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Speculative predictions gather context before their own model call but are normally background work until a matching caller joins them. Recorder-only collection is intentionally not awaited by prompt gathering. Either collector can nevertheless compete on the same event loop. Cancellation/timeout returns from the adapter and cancels its child token; late yielded snippets then hit the cancellation check.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke/pull the embedder stream with a child cancellation token
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per actual started speculative or recorder-enabled generation, with same-state callers joining upstream. No proven per-item host IPC operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: chat-lib had no embedder context stream for speculative or recording requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background when speculative/unjoined or recorder-only; can become awaited when a prediction joins, and ready streams still occupy the shared event loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the existing speculative model prediction and populate the existing suggestion cache
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per actual speculative generation attempt, shared by matching callers; existing scheduling/replacement governs multiplicity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same speculative prediction and joining mechanisms without chat-lib embedder context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Normally background prefetch; joined consumers depend on its result. New collection precedes issuance.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Actual speculative/ordinary generation attempts and N snippets per started collector. Matching document/post-edit state and cursor window coalesce consumers; not every facade getNextEdit call starts new work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One pending speculative is replaceable, while claimed requests can coexist for independent states/documents. A new ordinary pending request cancels its predecessor. Cooperative providers stop on the child token; no additional cross-document concurrency burst is proven. Provider-specific cancellation responsiveness is unknown.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Pending and claimed speculative requests remain discoverable for same-state joining and are released on completion. Existing positive and no-suggestion caches bypass fresh generation. An embedder unable to describe speculative text can yield nothing; the adapter supplies the exact existing snapshot without constructing a shadow workspace.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for traced cancellation, joining and background placement. The same ready-stream deadline bypass is established; no independent lifecycle leak or concurrency regression meets the reporting threshold.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider cooperation on cancellation and number of simultaneously claimed independent requests are external/workflow-dependent. Persistent resource leaks from noncooperative providers were not established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the single deadline-enforcement finding where ready streams block the event loop; no separate cancellation, retention or speculative-fan-out finding.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all seven changed-file diffs and relevant production callers, services, tests, caches, cancellation and expensive boundaries. Submitted one high-confidence deadline-bypass allocation/latency regression in the new chat-lib collector. VS Code collection is a refactor, unused integration remains cheap, and no concrete performance-regression fix requiring blame provenance was identified. Static review only; the external embedder implementation and runtime measurements were unavailable. The supporting performance-review guide tool returned only a truncated preview; learned mechanism guidance and the loaded focus instructions were available.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
